learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected disappears against stable intermediate share and takes over; locked it in.
observations.exploration: At generation 0, starts were 1% and 50%; latter had 25% young with two copies. +10 gave 4% and 15%. To gen 60 gave 13% for both, balance 13%. End on no-w-survival slider set 95%: generation 60 shares 4% and 5%, balance 5%. Home set 70%: both 23%, balance 23%; two-copy young 5%, one-copy young 36%.
observations.reveal: Corrected to stable intermediate share. Explained rare benefit versus common double-copy deaths, baseline 15/(15+100) ≈ 13%, and acknowledged 70% survival increases balance to 23%. Stated random mating, huge population and made-up species; named sickle-cell allele where malaria common with different numbers.
observations.visual: Actual 1257 × 936 dark screenshots inspected. Initial graph and later counters legible. Reveal opened an internal scrolling stage; graph top cropped in reveal screenshot and long answer heading runs close to right edge. No full reflow audit.

prediction.reason: Choices test eliminating a lethal variant versus maintaining a tradeoff.

interaction.reason: Contrasting starts and changed survival expose convergence and balance shift.

payoff.reason: Connects observed arrows and young-animal fractions to opposing selection, then tested parameter change.
payoff.evidence: Rare benefit/common death explanation and 70% acknowledgment.

clarity.reason: Controls and counters usable, but reveal internal scroll crops graph and packs lengthy text.
clarity.evidence: Actual reveal screenshot has cropped upper graph and near-edge heading.

transfer.reason: Concrete new biological example with environmental condition and differing-number caveat.
transfer.evidence: Sickle-cell allele where malaria common, with different numbers.

accessibility.reason: Only endpoint keys on one slider tested; insufficient audit.
accessibility.evidence: End/Home worked; focus order, contrast, phone, zoom and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Committed disappearance prediction contradicted by convergence to nonzero share.
surprise.evidence: Both starts at 13% despite double-copy death.

visualExplanation.reason: Two population curves and genotype fractions explain competing pulls.

playfulness.reason: Generation steps and slider endpoints expose reversible balance changes.

practicalValue.reason: Connects model to a concrete conditional biological example.

depth.reason: Frequency dependence, stable balance and changing selective advantage are linked.

complexity.reason: Coordinates allele share, genotype outcomes, selection and dynamic balance.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Several dependent relations: two copies, population frequency, reproductive survival and opposing long-run pulls.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Moderate: several data rows and internal reveal scroll.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: high: allele/genotype distinction and selection equilibrium.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: w notation, percentages, arrows and equilibrium ratio.

whyCool: Two very different starting shares converge, then moving survival shifts their shared destination from 13% to 23%.
caveat: Complex toy model with fixed mating and population assumptions; reveal layout requires internal scrolling and no fresh biological case is interactive.
missingEvidence: Intermediate generation-by-generation path beyond first ten not fully stepped.
Focus order, contrast, phone, zoom/reflow and motion untested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
